content:
Renowned economist Paul Krugman on Tuesday stressed that “treason” has been a key part of Nvidia’s business model and Donald Trump didn’t make an issue about the company’s scandal involving CEO Jensen Huang because he and those in his administration were “basically in on it.”

“This treasonous activity, trading with the enemy, selling critical technology to a U.S. adversary, was being done with the tacit approval of the Trump administration,” said Krugman, who won the 2008 Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences, in a video shared to his Substack page.

He later continued, “There’s no reason at all to believe that there won’t be more national security violations in the future.”

Krugman — who advised Americans “not to miss the forest for the sex,” a nod to Huang’s affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese spy — noted that Trump was reportedly briefed on Huang’s affair and the potential risks to national security over a year before the story broke but didn’t act on the information.

By the time news of the affair and alleged chip smuggling to China broke, prompting Huang’s resignation, Trump and Silicon Valley folks “moved heaven and earth” to ensure Huang faced “no consequences,” he argued.

Krugman went on, “So this was all just — if the right kind of guy is making money by endangering U.S. national security, well, what matters is who he is and not what he did.”

The economist later asked aloud why Trump, his administration and Silicon Valley didn’t make an issue of the scandal.

“Well, partly because if you’re a star, they let you do it,” said Krugman, referring to Trump’s infamous “Access Hollywood” comments.

Trump and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick were also “getting a cut one way or another” from the company, he added, with Lutnick “indirectly profiting” from Nvidia’s business and donating $25 million to Trump’s presidential library.

“[He] basically bribed Trump to avoid any consequences,” Krugman said.

“Trump himself clearly had some kind of stake. So there was just an extra layer of pretty raw corruption explaining this. And that also explains why Trump and company didn’t mind. The idea of profiting by selling out U.S. national security, well, that’s their kind of thing.”
